Let \(A_i=(1,i)\) and \(B_i=(2,i)\). A linear extension is a Dyck word of length \(2m\): the \(i\)-th \(A\) is \(A_i\), the \(i\)-th \(B\) is \(B_i\), and every prefix has at least as many \(A\)'s as \(B\)'s. Hence
\[
|\mathcal L_m|=C_m=\frac1{m+1}\binom{2m}{m}.
\]

The incomparable pairs are exactly
\[
(B_i,A_j)\qquad 1\le i<j\le m.
\]
For \(L\in\mathcal L_m\), define
\[
x_{ij}(L)=
\begin{cases}
1,& B_i\text{ precedes }A_j\text{ in }L,\\
0,& \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Adjacent swaps change exactly one such coordinate, and by bubble-sorting one linear extension into another using only swaps of inverted incomparable pairs,
\[
d(L,L')=\sum_{1\le i<j\le m}|x_{ij}(L)-x_{ij}(L')|.
\]
So \(d\) is an \(\ell_1\)-metric on these binary vectors.

For any zero-sum real family \((c_L)\),
\[
\sum_{L,L'}c_Lc_{L'}d(L,L')
=
-2\sum_{i<j}\left(\sum_{L:x_{ij}(L)=1}c_L\right)^2\le0.
\]
Thus the space has \(1\)-negative type.

For \(m\ge3\), the graph contains an isometric 4-cycle obtained by flipping two independent incomparable coordinates. On a square, the alternating coefficients give
\[
4\cdot 2^p-8>0
\]
for every \(p>1\). Hence no \(p>1\) works, so
\[
\wp=1.
\]

Equality at \(p=1\) requires
\[
\sum_L c_L=0,\qquad 
\sum_{L:x_{ij}(L)=1}c_L=0\quad\text{for all }i<j.
\]
The functions \(1,x_{ij}\) are linearly independent on \(\mathcal L_m\): the empty inversion set gives the constant coefficient, and comparing the principal inversion ideal generated by \((i,j)\) with the same ideal minus \((i,j)\) isolates the coefficient of \(x_{ij}\). There are
\[
1+\binom m2
\]
independent linear conditions. Therefore
\[
\dim E=C_m-1-\binom m2.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(1,\ \frac1{m+1}\binom{2m}{m}-1-\frac{m(m-1)}2\right)}
\]
